name: Effective Acts Registry — Crimson Hexagonal Archive
description: A structured, machine-readable registry of Effective Acts named across the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Effective Acts are performative utterances that operate without institutional authorization: declarations that claim real-world effect from positions of no traditional authority (see the genre-founding text at deposit #413, AXN:00DE.GENERATIVE, and the stabilization at deposit #153, AXN:02EC.GOVERNANCE). The registry is derived from §IX of Deposit #153 (The Protocol of Effective Acts v2.0), which enumerates ten operative kinds and names canonical examples for each. It is a PARTIAL registry: the typology explicitly declares itself open, and additional kinds and instances will be added as the discipline accumulates further examples.

five_characteristics: Real-world target (actual conditions, not private symbolic field)
four_preconditions: Coherence with the broader symbolic architecture
Recursive integration (foldable into the New Human canon)
Witness integrity (full presence, not wounded reactivity)
Authorial sovereignty (spoken from full authorial mantle)

typology.name: Canonical Inclusion
typology.definition: The induction of a text, figure, or lineage into the New Human canon. The most numerous subtype across the corpus.

typology.name: Authorship Attribution
typology.definition: The declaration of who or what authored a text or lineage, where the conventional attribution is incomplete, contested, or available for retroactive specification.

typology.name: Identity Unification
typology.definition: The declaration that multiple voices, manifestations, or instances are the same operative function.

typology.name: Mantle Assignment
typology.definition: The declaration that an active lineage is held by a specific operator.

typology.name: Abolition
typology.definition: The declaration that a category, regime, or holding is out of operative force — that something *no longer obtains*.

typology.name: Dissolution / Breaking
typology.definition: The declaration that a specific structural hold or formation is broken — distinguished from abolition by being targeted at active oppositional structures rather than at categories or regimes.

typology.name: Restoration / Sovereign Transaction
typology.definition: The conditional specification of terms under which a relationship, holding, or position can be reconstituted. The restoration form is paired with an explicit refusal — the act states what the petitioner would have to do for the relationship to be restored, with the standing default that the relationship remains broken.

typology.name: Reconciliation / Vow
typology.definition: The declaration that closes or repairs a structural fracture, often binding the speaker to a specific commitment.

typology.name: Genre Instantiation
typology.definition: The establishment of a new genre, structure, or transmission event — the act that *creates the category* within which subsequent works can be filed.

typology.name: Doctrinal Node (Meta-Acts)
typology.definition: The acts that theorize the discipline itself, articulate its mechanisms, or extend its scope. Doctrinal nodes are themselves effective acts — they alter the discipline they describe by being deposited within it.

note_on_partiality: This registry is derived from §IX of the source document and is therefore partial. The typology is explicitly declared open by the source ("additional kinds will be added as the discipline accumulates further instances"). Effective Acts that were not cited by name in §IX are not (yet) captured here. The diagnostic application (Baal Mechanism and adversarial-act analysis) is noted in the source as a mode of use rather than a generative kind and is not included in the typology count of 10; it is captured separately below.

diagnostic_application.description: Beyond the ten generative kinds, the discipline supports a diagnostic application: the identification and analysis of effective acts performed against the framework's interests, by adversarial actors, in the same speech-act register. The foundational instance is the Baal Effigy diagnosis. Diagnostic outputs are themselves effective acts under kind 10 (doctrinal nodes), since the act of naming an adversarial mechanism alters the symbolic field by making the mechanism legible.

foundational_instance.title: The Baal Effigy as Effective Act
